items.title: Periodic responses of $\ddot z=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$ and the affine classification of all solutions
items.reference: scaffold-added necessary mathematical prerequisite for the weak-field Thomson item (see research/physics-em-sr-40-2026-10-08-batch-40.notes.md)
items.statement: Let $\omega>0$, $T:=2\pi/\omega$, $n\ge1$ and $w\in\mathbb C^n$; use the real part and complex exponential of [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]] and [[def-complex-exponential]]. Define $z_p:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^n$ by $z_p(t):=\operatorname{Re}(-w\omega^{-2}e^{-i\omega t})$ componentwise ([[def-derivative]] for the derivative below). Then: (a) $z_p$ is $C^\infty$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) and satisfies $z_p''(t)=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$; it is $T$-periodic. (b) every $C^2$ solution $z:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^n$ of $z''(t)=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$ on $\mathbb R$ has the form $z(t)=z_p(t)+a+bt$ with unique $a,b\in\mathbb R^n$. (c) such a solution is $T$-periodic if and only if $b=0$; the $T$-periodic solutions are exactly $z_p(t)+a$, $a\in\mathbb R^n$, and their oscillating part has complex amplitude $-w/\omega^2$. (d) [Local solutions and exact global extension] Let I be any nonempty open interval, t* in I, and let z:I->R^n be C2 with the same harmonic equation on I. Then z=z_p+a+bt on I for a UNIQUE pair a,b, with b=z'(t*)-z_p'(t*) and a=z(t*)-z_p(t*)-bt*. The same explicit formula defines its unique global harmonic-ODE extension Z on R. This extension is T-periodic exactly when b0, equivalently z'(t*)=z_p'(t*); when b0 its mean over every complete period is a. For general drift, the mean of its global extension over [t,t+T] is a+b(t+T/2). Thus periodic preparation can be imposed on the global response without requiring a driven nonlinear family to exist on R. If I contains at least one pair t,t+T, equality at that pair forces b0. If I contains no such pair, a condition expressed only as z(t+T)=z(t) wherever both arguments belong to I is vacuous and does not imply periodicity of the global extension. All affine-drift local solutions remain classified, and the original global branches(a)-(c) remain intact.
items.strategy: (a) By the Cartesian form and Euler identity of [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]], $z_p(t)=-\omega^{-2}[(\operatorname{Re}w)\cos(\omega t)+(\operatorname{Im}w)\sin(\omega t)]$ componentwise. Differentiating twice with the sum, scalar-multiple and product rules of [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] and the derivatives of [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]] gives $z_p''=\operatorname{Re}w\cos(\omega t)+\operatorname{Im}w\sin(\omega t)=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$. Periodicity of $z_p$ follows from $e^{-i\omega(t+T)}=e^{-i\omega t}e^{-i\omega T}=e^{-i\omega t}$ by the addition law of [[thm-complex-exponential-addition-and-real-extension]] and $e^{-2\pi i}=1$, the latter from the Cartesian form and the values $\cos2\pi=1$, $\sin2\pi=0$ of [[thm-sine-cosine-zero-sets-and-fundamental-period]]. (b) If $z$ is any $C^2$ solution, then $h:=z-z_p$ satisfies $h''=0$ on $\mathbb R$. Apply [[cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant]] on the interval $\mathbb R$ ([[def-interval]]) to each component of $h'$: $h'=b$ is constant. Applying the same corollary to $h-b\,\mathrm{id}$ gives $h=a+bt$, and consequently $z=z_p+a+bt$. Uniqueness of $a,b$ from $z(0)$ and $z'(0)$ is immediate. (c) If $b=0$ then $z=z_p+a$ is $T$-periodic by (a). Conversely, if $z$ is $T$-periodic then $z(t+T)-z(t)=bT$ for all $t$, hence $b=0$; then $z-z_p=a$ is the constant part whose complex amplitude is zero, while the oscillating part $z_p$ has complex amplitude $-w/\omega^2$ by construction. No choice principle is used. For(d), apply the zero-derivative corollary on each closed subinterval of I to h'=z'-z_p', then to h-b id; any two points of the interval are contained in such a subinterval, so the constants agree throughout I. Evaluate at t* to get the displayed a,b, proving uniqueness. The explicit global formula is a solution on R by(a), and every other global solution extending z has the same value and derivative at t*, hence the same affine constants. Its period increment is bT, giving the periodicity equivalences and the single-pair test. The harmonic sine/cosine part integrates to zero over a complete period by scalar FTC, so its mean is a. This last claim uses only ordinary finite-period integrals and no choice. The derivatives in(a) use the total chain rule [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]] componentwise (or scalar coordinate-line chain rules), not a derivative rule asserted by the exponential definition alone.

items.title: The ideal harmonic electric-dipole radiation model
items.reference: scaffold-added necessary model definition for the dipole scattering and Thomson items (see research/physics-em-sr-40-2026-10-08-batch-40.notes.md)
items.statement: Let $\omega>0$, $k:=\omega/c$ with $c$ the vacuum speed of [[def-em-si-conventions]], $\mu_0>0$ the vacuum permeability of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and $p_0\in\mathbb C^3$ (the complex dipole-moment amplitude, in $\mathrm C\,\mathrm m$). Define, on the punctured space $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ and all times $t\in\mathbb R$, $$E_{\rm d}(x,t):=\operatorname{Re}\Bigl(-\frac{\mu_0\omega^2}{4\pi r}\,n\times(n\times p_0)\,e^{i(kr-\omega t)}\Bigr),\qquad B_{\rm d}(x,t):=\frac1c\,n\times E_{\rm d}(x,t),$$ where $r:=|x|$ and $n:=x/r$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]), with the real part and complex exponential of [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]] and [[def-complex-exponential]] and the componentwise real-part encoding convention of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]] (the spatial amplitude here varies with x; no plane-wave instance is asserted). Call $(E_{\rm d},B_{\rm d})$ the **ideal harmonic electric-dipole radiation model of frequency $\omega$ and amplitude $p_0$**, and call $S_{\rm d}:=E_{\rm d}\times B_{\rm d}/\mu_0$ its model flux ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]]); the model fields are read as an electric and a magnetic field of [[def-em-fields]]. [Adopted status] This is an explicitly adopted ideal radiation-law model, fixed by the following declarations: (i) it is the leading transverse far-zone field of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]](c) evaluated at the harmonic transverse moment $V(u)=\operatorname{Re}(-\omega^2p_0e^{-i\omega u})$, i.e. at $p''$ for the waveform $p(u)=\operatorname{Re}(p_0e^{-i\omega u})$; (ii) the model contains no independent magnetic-dipole or higher-multipole radiation, no near-zone or static field and no other radiating component; (iii) it is not asserted to solve the vacuum Maxwell equations at finite $r$, to be the field of any actual source, to satisfy any boundary condition or to have finite total energy on $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$; (iv) for compact smooth conserved sources, comparison with these prescribed model fields uses the actual source's moment p_act(u), the harmonic waveform p_h(u)=Re(p0 exp(-i omega u)), their second-derivative mismatch M(u)=|p_act''(u)-p_h''(u)|, and the explicit D,Gamma bounds of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]]. A bound depending only on that source's D and Gamma is valid when M0 on the observation window; the source's moment is not automatically the independently prescribed p0. These actual-source comparison uses assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) carried by the cited theorem. The explicit ideal fields themselves and their pointwise flux definition remain choice-free. No measured, empirical or material-response content is adopted: $p_0$ is prescribed model data, not a derived polarizability.
items.strategy: This is a definition contract; well-definedness is discharged by the cited suppliers. (i) The formula is the leading transverse term $E_{\rm lead}=\mu_0n\times(n\times V)/(4\pi r)$ of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]](c) at $V(u)=\operatorname{Re}(-\omega^2p_0e^{-i\omega u})$: since $p''(u)=\operatorname{Re}(-\omega^2p_0e^{-i\omega u})$ for $p(u)=\operatorname{Re}(p_0e^{-i\omega u})$, the derivative supplied by [[lem-em-harmonic-forcing-periodic-response]](a) with w=-omega²p0, using its explicit C-infinity real harmonic waveform, the model field is exactly $E_{\rm lead}$ rewritten with $u=t-r/c$ and $e^{i(kr-\omega t)}=e^{-i\omega(t-r/c)}$; the cross product, inner product and norm are those of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]] and [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. (ii) $r>0$ on the declared domain, so $E_{\rm d}$ and $B_{\rm d}$ are $C^\infty$ there and the same componentwise real-part convention as [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]] is used; the varying radial amplitude is not a plane-wave amplitude; $E_{\rm d}\cdot n=0$ because $n\times(n\times p_0)$ is orthogonal to $n$, and $B_{\rm d}=n\times E_{\rm d}/c$ by definition. (iii) The model flux $S_{\rm d}$ is the quantity of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]] evaluated at the model fields; that definition applies to any pair of fields of the declared regularity and assigns no field equation. (iv) The status clause lists the model assumptions (i)-(iv) and excludes exact Maxwell, source-realization, boundary, finite-energy and empirical claims; the model's relation to actual sources is only through the explicit bounds of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]], which are quantified in the item below. The explicit formula/flux construction uses no choice. Actual compact-source comparisons retain the stated Countable Choice of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]], including a moment-mismatch term; no comparison to an arbitrary unrelated harmonic amplitude follows from D alone. Smoothness off r0 follows by coordinate sum/product/chain rules and the positive square-root/reciprocal powers of [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]] for r=|x|; The harmonic lemma supplies all derivatives of the real waveform; compose its second derivative with u=t-r/c using the declared total chain rule. No complex-to-real derivative theorem is silently substituted for that real-waveform interface. Orthogonality is the finite cross-product identity of [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]] applied separately to real and imaginary components. The ideal model is meaningful also at p0=0, giving zero fields; no actual source realization or finite-radius Maxwell equation is deduced.

items.physical_scope: Explicit ideal radiation-law model of a harmonic electric dipole of complex amplitude $p_0$ in vacuum: the leading transverse far-zone fields $E_{\rm d},B_{\rm d}$ on the punctured space, their flux $S_{\rm d}$, and the declared absence of magnetic-dipole and higher-multipole content. Excluded: exact Maxwell solutions at finite radius, near-zone and static fields, any actual source construction, boundary conditions, finite total energy, self-force and radiation reaction, material response laws, and every measured or empirical statement; the relation to actual compact smooth sources is only through the explicit error bounds of the dipole theorem.

items.title: Differential and total cross sections of the ideal harmonic dipole in a plane-wave field
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]] and [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]] ([[def-countable-choice]]); the period-average and cross-section algebra itself uses no choice. Adopt the ideal harmonic electric-dipole radiation model of [[def-em-ideal-harmonic-dipole-model]] with frequency $\omega>0$, wavenumber $k=\omega/c$ and amplitude $p_0\in\mathbb C^3$; let $E_{\rm d},B_{\rm d},S_{\rm d}$ be its fields and model flux. Let $\kappa\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ with $|\kappa|=\omega/c$, $e\in\mathbb C^3\setminus\{0\}$ with $\kappa\cdot e=0$, $b:=\kappa\times e/\omega$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), and let $(E_{\rm inc},B_{\rm inc})$ be the corresponding plane-wave fields of [[def-em-plane-wave-definition]] on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$; by [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]] they satisfy the smooth-branch source-free vacuum Maxwell equations, and by [[pthm-em-wave-energy-average]](b) their period-averaged energy flux has magnitude $I_{\rm inc}=\frac{\varepsilon_0c}{2}|e|^2=\frac{|e|^2}{2\mu_0c}$ ([[def-em-si-conventions]]). Define the **model differential scattering cross section** by $$\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(n):=\frac{r^2\langle S_{\rm d}(rn,\cdot)\cdot n\rangle}{\langle S_{\rm inc}\cdot\hat\kappa\rangle},\qquad n\in S^2,\ r>0,$$ where $\hat\kappa:=\kappa/|\kappa|$, $S_{\rm inc}:=E_{\rm inc}\times B_{\rm inc}/\mu_0$ ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]]), and $\langle f\rangle:=\frac1T\int_0^Tf(s)\,ds$, $T=2\pi/\omega$, is the period average at fixed observation point. Then: (a) [Angular pattern] the ratio is independent of $r$ and of the averaging start, and for every $n\in S^2$ $$\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(n)=\frac{\omega^4|n\times p_0|^2}{16\pi^2\varepsilon_0^2c^4|e|^2}=\frac{\mu_0^2\omega^4|n\times p_0|^2}{16\pi^2|e|^2}.$$ (b) [Total cross section] with $d\sigma_{S^2}$ the surface measure of the unit sphere, $\sigma:=\int_{S^2}\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}\,d\sigma_{S^2}$ equals $$\sigma=\frac{\omega^4|p_0|^2}{6\pi\varepsilon_0^2c^4|e|^2}=\frac{\mu_0^2\omega^4|p_0|^2}{6\pi|e|^2};$$ if $p_0=\alpha e$ for a complex scalar $\alpha$ (the scalar polarizability, in $\mathrm F\,\mathrm m^2$), then $\sigma=\frac{\omega^4|\alpha|^2}{6\pi\varepsilon_0^2c^4}$ and $\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(n)=\frac{\omega^4|\alpha|^2}{16\pi^2\varepsilon_0^2c^4}|n\times\hat e|^2$ with $\hat e:=e/|e|$. (c) [Fidelity for arbitrary actual sources and matched windows] Let an actual compact smooth conserved source satisfy the exact hypotheses of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]], with spatial support radius a>0, source-time interval [tau0,tau1], moment p_act(u), variation bound D(u) and constants Gamma_E,Gamma_B. These source data are independent of the prescribed model amplitude p0. Put
$$p_h(u):=\operatorname{Re}(p_0e^{-i\omega u}),\qquad M(u):=|p_{\rm act}''(u)-p_h''(u)|.$$
For n in S2,u in[tau0,tau1],r>=2a, define
$$H(u,r):=\frac{\Gamma_E}{r^2}+\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi r}[D(u)+M(u)].$$
The actual retarded fields and the model fields satisfy, uniformly in n,
$$|E_{\rm act}(rn,u+r/c)-E_{\rm d}(rn,u+r/c)|\le H(u,r),$$
$$|B_{\rm act}(rn,u+r/c)-B_{\rm d}(rn,u+r/c)|\le\frac{\Gamma_B+\Gamma_E/c}{r^2}+\frac{H(u,r)}c.$$
Also retain the sharper direct source-leading-field consequence
$$|B_{\rm act}-B_{\rm d}|\le\frac{\Gamma_B}{r^2}+\frac{\mu_0[D(u)+M(u)]}{4\pi cr}$$
at the same events. If p_act''=p_h'' on a specified finite window, M0 there and these give the full matched dipole bounds; in particular they imply the older coarser electric bound Gamma_E/r²+mu0 D/(2pi r). Neither moment matching nor D0 is automatic. A sound sufficient matched branch is p_act=p_h+a0+b0 u on an open neighborhood of the window (any fixed real vectors a0,b0). Such a branch has actual compact realizations over any finite window: choose a smooth time cutoff eta equal1 near the window, let p_eta=eta(p_h+a0+b0 u), choose a nonnegative smooth spatial bump sigma with support inside B_a and integral1, and set rho=-p_eta dot grad sigma,J=p_eta' sigma. Then continuity holds and the actual moment is p_eta; outside the window it is tapered. Apply the actual theorem with the resulting D and Gamma, retaining every finite-radius/source-variation error. No eternal harmonic moment of a compact-time source is asserted. (d) [Scope] conditional predictions of the adopted ideal model: no measured cross section, no frequency-domain response law (the amplitude $p_0$ is prescribed model data), no magnetic-dipole or higher-multipole content, no self-force, material response, finite-size or empirical claim; the scalar-$\alpha$ clause records a declared proportional response, not a derived polarizability. In all complex-amplitude formulas |v|²=sum_i |v_i|² is the Hermitian norm square; n cross v is complex-linear for real n. The p0=0 case gives zero scattered fields and cross sections while the nonzero incident intensity still defines the ratios. Actual-source fidelity assumes only the explicitly quantified mismatch and source hypotheses; it does not turn the model cross section into a measured or self-consistent scattering prediction.
items.strategy: (a) In the model, $B_{\rm d}=n\times E_{\rm d}/c$ and $n\cdot E_{\rm d}=0$, so $S_{\rm d}\cdot n=n\cdot(E_{\rm d}\times(n\times E_{\rm d}))/(\mu_0c)=|E_{\rm d}|^2/(\mu_0c)$ pointwise; writing $w:=-\frac{\mu_0\omega^2}{4\pi r}n\times(n\times p_0)e^{ikr}$, the model has $E_{\rm d}=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$, and [[lem-em-period-average]] gives $\langle|E_{\rm d}|^2\rangle=\frac12|w|^2=\frac{\mu_0^2\omega^4}{32\pi^2r^2}|n\times p_0|^2$ ([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]], [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]]). Hence $r^2\langle S_{\rm d}\cdot n\rangle=\frac{\mu_0\omega^4}{32\pi^2c}|n\times p_0|^2$, independent of $r$ and of the averaging start. Division by the incident flux $I_{\rm inc}=\frac{|e|^2}{2\mu_0c}$ of [[pthm-em-wave-energy-average]](b) and $\mu_0^2=\frac1{\varepsilon_0^2c^4}$ ([[def-em-si-conventions]]) give the two displayed forms. (b) [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]](d) gives $\int_{S^2}|n\times a|^2d\sigma=\frac{8\pi}3|a|^2$ for real $a$, and applying it to the real and imaginary parts of $p_0$ gives the complex case; integrating the pattern of (a) over $S^2$ yields $\frac{\mu_0^2\omega^4}{16\pi^2|e|^2}\cdot\frac{8\pi}3|p_0|^2=\frac{\mu_0^2\omega^4|p_0|^2}{6\pi|e|^2}$, i.e. the two displayed forms. For $p_0=\alpha e$ substitute $|p_0|^2=|\alpha|^2|e|^2$ and $|n\times p_0|^2=|\alpha|^2|e|^2|n\times\hat e|^2$ ([[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]]). (c) At t=u+r/c the SIGNED model leading field is mu0 n cross(n cross p_h''(u))/(4pi r). The actual source theorem bounds E_act against the leading field of p_act'' by Gamma_E/r²+mu0 D/(4pi r). The real unit-direction double-cross projection has norm at most1, so the difference of the two leading fields is bounded by mu0 M/(4pi r). Adding gives H, including the zero actual source countercheck: then D=Gamma0 but M=|p_h''|, which exactly accounts for a nonzero prescribed model. The source theorem's B-n cross E_act/c bound is (Gamma_B+Gamma_E/c)/r²; add c^-1 times H to obtain the retained magnetic bound. Separately its stronger B-leading(V_act) estimate is Gamma_B/r²; |V_act-p_h''|<=D+M gives the sharper direct magnetic estimate. For the compact-window construction, smooth nonnegative cutoffs from [[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]] may be normalized and scaled to give sigma ([[def-mollifier-family-generated-by-a-unit-mass-smooth-bump]] for the scaling convention). Continuity is rho_t=-p_eta' dot grad sigma and div J=p_eta' dot grad sigma. Integration by parts on a bounding rectangle gives integral rho0 and integral y_i rho=(p_eta)_i integral sigma=(p_eta)_i, using [[thm-integration-by-parts]], [[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]] and the Countable-Choice comparison [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]]. Choose source-time endpoints outside the taper support, so all compact smooth hypotheses are met. Moment matching on the window removes M, but D and Gamma remain the actual finite-source quantities. (d) records the scope; no measured or material content is added ([[def-em-si-conventions]] only fixes units and constants). No choice principle beyond that carried by [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]] and [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]] (Countable Choice, as stated there) is used. The Countable Choice hypothesis is inherited from the actual compact-source and sphere-moment suppliers; the finite period-average calculation and cross-section algebra are choice-free. Complex norms mean |v|²=sum_i |v_i|². Real unit n acts complex-linearly by cross products; all norm identities used in(a),(b) follow by summing the real and imaginary norm identities. The minus sign in w agrees with the model definition; squaring for its flux does not erase a sign mismatch in the field identity. Period averaging adds no choice; Countable Choice here is precisely the actual source/sphere-integral premise.

items.physical_scope: Conditional cross sections of the ideal harmonic electric-dipole model in a prescribed incident plane wave: the differential pattern $\frac{\omega^4|n\times p_0|^2}{16\pi^2\varepsilon_0^2c^4|e|^2}$, the total cross section and its scalar-polarizability specialization, together with the explicit absolute fidelity bounds to actual compact smooth sources inherited from the dipole theorem. Excluded: measured or source-backed cross sections, derived polarizabilities or response laws, magnetic-dipole and higher-multipole content, self-force, radiation reaction, material and finite-size models, and all empirical or statistical claims.

items.title: Controlled first variation of the relativistic test-charge law: the leading Thomson-model cross section
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by [[pthm-em-dipole-scattering-cross-section]]; the linearization below and [[lem-em-harmonic-forcing-periodic-response]] use no choice. Assume the setting and postulates of [[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]] for a test particle with charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$ ([[def-em-sources]](a)) and externally supplied rest mass $m>0$, in the incident plane-wave field of [[def-em-plane-wave-definition]] with wavevector $\kappa$, complex amplitude $e\ne0$, $\kappa\cdot e=0$, $|\kappa|=\omega/c$ and $b=\kappa\times e/\omega$ as in [[pthm-em-dipole-scattering-cross-section]]; write $E_{\rm inc}(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(e\,e^{i(\kappa\cdot x-\omega t)})$ and $B_{\rm inc}=\kappa\times E_{\rm inc}/\omega$ ([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-si-conventions]]). Assume that for some $\eta_0>0$ and a common open interval $I\ni0$, for every $\eta\in(-\eta_0,\eta_0)$ there is a $C^2$ future timelike massive solution $r_\eta:I\to\mathbb R^3$ of the adopted four-force law in the external field $\eta(E_{\rm inc},B_{\rm inc})$ (no self-field, recoil or material force), and that the family admits a uniform first-order expansion: there are $r_1\in C^2(I;\mathbb R^3)$ and, for every compact $K\subset I$, a constant $C_K$ with $$|r_\eta(t)-x_0-\eta r_1(t)|+|\dot r_\eta(t)-\eta\dot r_1(t)|\le C_K\eta^2\qquad(t\in K,\ |\eta|<\eta_0)$$ about a fixed position $x_0\in\mathbb R^3$, The family time interval I is not required to contain a full period, and no solution r_eta outside I is assumed. For the periodic-response conclusions(b),(c), impose the following explicit preparation(P): the unique global harmonic-ODE extension of r1 supplied after(a) by [[lem-em-harmonic-forcing-periodic-response]](d), with its actual value and derivative at0, is T-periodic, T=2pi/omega. Equivalently its affine drift is zero, or $r_1'(0)=\operatorname{Re}(iw/\omega)$ with $w=(q/m)e e^{i\kappa\cdot x_0}$. The linearized equation and affine local/global classification in(a) hold for every stated family even without(P); overlap-only periodicity on a short I is not substituted for(P). Then: (a) [Linearized equation] $\ddot r_1(t)=\frac qmE_{\rm inc}(x_0,t)=\frac qm\operatorname{Re}(e\,e^{i(\kappa\cdot x_0-\omega t)})$ on $I$. (b) [Induced dipole under preparation(P)] $x_0$ is the zeroth-order rest/reference position. Let a be the mean of the global periodic first-order response, so on I one has r1=z_p+a. The arbitrary constant a is retained: no exact mean or periodicity of the full nonlinear family is asserted. The oscillating part of the first-order dipole coefficient $q(r_1-a)$ is $\operatorname{Re}(p_0e^{-i\omega t})$ with complex amplitude $$p_0=-\frac{q^2}{m\omega^2}\,e\,e^{i\kappa\cdot x_0};$$ equivalently $p_0=\alpha e'$ with $\alpha=-\frac{q^2}{m\omega^2}$ (units $\mathrm F\,\mathrm m^2$) and the unimodular factor $e'=e\,e^{i\kappa\cdot x_0}$, $|e'|=|e|$. (c) [Leading Thomson-model cross section] substituting this $p_0$ into [[pthm-em-dipole-scattering-cross-section]](b) gives $$\sigma_{\rm T}=\frac{q^4}{6\pi\varepsilon_0^2m^2c^4}=\frac{8\pi}{3}\Bigl(\frac{q^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0mc^2}\Bigr)^2,$$ independent of $\omega$ and of the phase factor. (d) [Scope] this is a controlled conditional first variation of the adopted relativistic external-force law under the stated solution-family hypotheses. It is not the exact Newtonian force postulate, it does not assert existence, persistence, stability or self-consistency of the family, it excludes self-force, radiation reaction and material media, and it makes no empirical, measurement, atomic-physics or frequency-response claim. In(a), every local r1 has the unique global harmonic extension z_p+a+bt, with z_p=Re(-w omega^-2 exp(-i omega t)), b=r1'(0)-z_p'(0), a=r1(0)-z_p(0). Thus the general affine-drift response is also retained; preparation(P) sets b0 for(b),(c) and leaves a arbitrary. For a nonzero eta, the associated LEADING ideal harmonic model has incident amplitude eta e and induced dipole amplitude eta p0. Their squared flux factors eta² cancel in its cross-section ratio; sigma_T is this leading-model coefficient, not an assertion of the exact nonlinear particle's emitted field or cross section. At q0 the induced amplitude and sigma_T are zero without any division by q. All eta estimates apply only to the open parameter domain on which the family was declared.
items.strategy:
Use the exact integrated momentum ODE; never differentiate a uniform-in-time Oeta² remainder. Fix a compact K in I and choose a closed interval L contained in I that contains K and0. Put v_eta=r_eta', gamma_eta=(1-|v_eta|²/c²)^-1/2, and P_eta=m gamma_eta v_eta. The stated family expansion implies r_eta->x0 and v_eta/eta->r1' uniformly on L as eta->0 with eta!=0, and |v_eta|=O(|eta|). For small eta the fixed speed bound |v_eta|/c<=1/2 holds on L; the actual algebraic low-speed clause of [[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]] gives gamma_eta=1+O(eta²) uniformly. Hence P_eta/eta->m r1' uniformly, using only multiplication of uniformly bounded functions.
The EXACT coordinate ODE of that supplier is
$$P_\eta'(t)=q\eta\,[E_{\rm inc}(r_\eta(t),t)+v_\eta(t)\times B_{\rm inc}(r_\eta(t),t)].$$
The plane-wave fields are smooth with bounded spatial first derivatives on a common compact tube around x0 times L, so their values at r_eta converge uniformly to their values at x0; the magnetic term is uniformly Oeta since B is bounded and v_eta=Oeta. Thus for eta!=0, P_eta'/eta converges uniformly to q E_inc(x0,t). This derivative convergence comes from the adopted ODE, not from differentiating the family expansion. Apply componentwise scalar FTC [[thm-ftc-second-part]] to the actual C1 momentum on [0,t], with oriented limits for t<0:
$$\frac{P_\eta(t)-P_\eta(0)}\eta=q\int_0^t[E_{\rm inc}(r_\eta(s),s)+v_\eta(s)\times B_{\rm inc}(r_\eta(s),s)]ds.$$
Uniform convergence passes through these finite ordinary integrals: each component's error is at most the interval length times its uniform supremum, by [[lem-integral-elementary-bounds]]. Taking the limit gives
$$m[r_1'(t)-r_1'(0)]=q\int_0^tE_{\rm inc}(x_0,s)ds.$$
The continuous integrand and [[thm-ftc-first-part]] now imply m r1''=q E_inc(x0,t) on I. This proves(a) and the available first-order equation while retaining the original position/velocity assumptions and arbitrary local I; no differentiability in eta beyond the given uniform expansion and no acceleration-error differentiation is assumed. The parameter endpoints eta=+-eta0 are never evaluated. A continuous differentiable family was not replaced by a stronger C2-in-eta family.
By the LOCAL interval/global extension clause(d) of [[lem-em-harmonic-forcing-periodic-response]] with w=(q/m)e exp(i kappa dot x0), r1=z_p+a+bt on I and its explicit extension on R is unique. Preparation(P) says this extension is periodic, hence b0; this is nonvacuous even when I is shorter than a period. Its mean a comes from the harmonic lemma's finite-period mean calculation. Therefore q(r1-a)=Re[-q² e exp(i kappa dot x0) exp(-i omega t)/(m omega²)], proving(b), with the arbitrary constant mean retained and x0 only the zeroth-order reference position. The phase factor has modulus1 by [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]], so |p0|=q²|e|/(m omega²) and p0=alpha e', alpha=-q²/(m omega²).
Substituting into [[pthm-em-dipole-scattering-cross-section]](b) cancels omega^4 and gives sigma_T=q^4/(6pi epsilon0²m²c^4)=(8pi/3)[q²/(4pi epsilon0 m c²)]². The formula is for the leading ideal harmonic model: for nonzero eta scale BOTH incident amplitude and harmonic dipole amplitude by eta, so their ratio is unchanged. At q0 the same algebra gives zero response amplitude and zero cross section. The adopted external-force law excludes self-field and material/recoil forces; neither the local solution-family assumption nor the global extension of its LINEAR response proves global persistence/periodicity of the nonlinear family or a self-consistent scattered field. Finite-interval FTC, uniform limits and harmonic affine classification are choice-free; only the stated cross-section source/sphere premise carries Countable Choice.

items.physical_scope: Conditional weak-field (small-amplitude) first variation of the adopted relativistic external-force law for a test charge in an ideal plane wave: the linearized periodic displacement, the induced harmonic dipole amplitude $p_0=-\frac{q^2}{m\omega^2}e e^{i\kappa\cdot x_0}$, and the resulting leading Thomson-model cross section $\frac{q^4}{6\pi\varepsilon_0^2m^2c^4}$ independent of frequency. Excluded: exact Newtonian force laws, existence, persistence, stability or self-consistency of the weak-field family, self-force and radiation reaction, material media, quantum and atomic-resonance content, and every measured, statistical or empirical claim. The nonlinear family remains on any common open I containing0; only its harmonic first-order ODE response is globally extended and periodically prepared. x0 is a zeroth-order rest/reference position, with arbitrary first-order response mean a; no exact nonlinear-family mean/periodicity is claimed. All zero-charge and complex-polarization cases remain.
